provenance.note: Measured after the NCC hot-loop change (b1d74bf): four accumulator chains in prepare_chip! and integral_both!, ifelse for the denominator guard, and FFTW_PATIENT plans. Compare rows by cores used, not by runtime alone. This run achieved 2.91 cores on the 12-thread eager row against 3.78 for the previous run at 8d7c1ec, so that row is 33.2 s against 25.6 s despite strictly less work per point -- the machine was busier, not the code slower. The python row moved the same way, 193.2 s against 177.5 at 2.17 cores against 2.35, on a reference that cannot have changed, which is what identifies the cause as contention. The comparable rows are the two that ran at ~1.0 cores in both runs: eager 1 thread is 67.2 s against 79.5, a 1.18x speedup, which is the honest end-to-end figure for the change. The binary rows are flat because this binary was rebuilt from the same source but its 8d7c1ec counterpart was not the bottleneck being measured -- block size is, and those ratios hold within a run. The 4096 lazy row peaked at 10291 MiB against 3637 at 2048: 25 blocks on 12 threads holds twelve 6144-pixel working sets at once, which measures the block size being large relative to the scene rather than what blocking costs. 8192 is excluded for the same reason at 9 blocks.
